brief: A small-parts organizer with at least six separate bins.

requirements.evidence: Six hex-bin-half bins, one in each of the six base cells: bin:-1,0,0, bin:0,-1,0, bin:0,0,0, bin:1,-1,0, bin:-1,1,0, bin:1,0,0.
The bins are half depth so small parts are easy to reach, and they sit in a compact 6-cell cluster. Shown with M3 hardware, a solder reel and tape in the bins. Ends are capped and joints bolted.

finish.summary: I built a small-parts organizer from six hex base cells in a compact cluster. Each cell holds its own half-depth bin, so there are six separate bins. All open faces are capped and the joints are bolted. To show it in use, I put M3 screws, nuts, standoffs, a solder reel and electrical tape in the bins. The parts sit below the bin rims, so you can't see them from the side, but they all show from above. The build check passed with no rule issues, no prop warnings and no mesh collisions. The parts list comes to 30 parts, about 2.6 kg of filament and roughly 62 hours of printing.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
